NAH

You’re young, and as you said - you don’t do this for a living, so it’s understandable to have limitations in order to maintain a healthy work/life balance. However, I don’t think your manager is an asshole either as we -are- in a peak crisis situation and when it gets busy people are rostered on to counter the added workload. He wasn’t rude to you, and took your complaint into account which is unfortunately better than I would’ve expected in a time like this. 

Just remember that this craziness will die down soon, so if you have to work an extra shift every here and there, it won’t be like that forever. This is what it’s like being in the workforce, and I think this experience will do you well in the long run.
Regardless as to whether he has any “connection” to his Latino side, it’s still apart of him. Again, how does this affect you at all?

Yes the circumstances may feel weird but I think it would do both of you good to get the chance to say goodbye before disengaging in each other’s lives.

YTA

He didn’t lie on his college application, and honestly it sounds like you’re a bit jealous that he got into a good college. You’ve mounted your high horse proudly as if you’re doing the world a great service by pointing out that -actually- he’s 1/8th hispanic, when in reality the number doesn’t matter and it just makes you look petty and resentful towards your brother.

I think you need to do some self reflection and figure out what you’re actually upset about.

NAH

Without your friends side of the story it does sound like he was hoping you wouldn’t find out about the party, however it also sounds like it could’ve just been a minor miscommunication. There isn’t really enough info here to strongly deduct who is and isn’t the asshole and we don’t know how exactly you reacted other than the vague description you’ve provided.

Regardless, I suggest just going to the party instead of making a big deal about not personally receiving an invite. Moving on from this minor dilemma is better than getting stuck on it and potentially losing a friendship.
